name: RVC WebUI (Retrieval-based Voice Conversion)
description: Retrieval-based-Voice-Conversion-WebUI (RVC-Project) — a Gradio-based voice-conversion / voice-cloning trainer and inference UI. Trains a speaker-timbre model from <=10 minutes of target voice data and converts any input speech into the target voice, preserving intonation. Entry point infer-web.py launches a Gradio Blocks app on port 7865. Tabs cover model inference, one-click training, ckpt processing, and UVR5 vocal separation. Gradio provides no authentication unless auth= is passed to launch(), which the upstream repo does not set.
auth_notes: infer-web.py calls app.launch() with no auth= argument, so the Gradio WebUI on port 7865 is fully unauthenticated when server_name is set to 0.0.0.0 (common in Docker/cloud runs). Anyone reaching the port can run inference, upload training audio, kick off training jobs, and browse the file/model dropdowns. The repo also supports launching with --share, producing a public *.gradio.live tunnel that bypasses any host firewall entirely. No API key, no session, no login form. The only barrier in default deployments is network reachability.

shodan_dorks.rationale: Default RVC Gradio port; broad Gradio marker. High recall, but shares 7865/gradio signal with other Gradio apps — always pair with a strict tier to confirm RVC
Project name string rendered in the Gradio markdown header; disambiguates RVC from Applio/OpenVoice/other Gradio apps

shodan_dorks.query: port:7865 http.html:"gradio" http.html:"Model Inference" http.html:"ckpt Processing"

known_vulns: Gradio WebUI launched without auth= — unauthenticated inference, training-audio upload, and job control on port 7865
--share mode publishes a public *.gradio.live tunnel that bypasses host/cloud firewalls entirely
Gradio CVE-2023-51449 — path traversal in the /file endpoint (Gradio <4.11.0) leaks arbitrary host files including /proc/self/environ
Gradio CVE-2024-1561 — arbitrary local file read via /component_server method invocation (Gradio 4.3-4.12); reads secrets and model files
Gradio CVE-2024-1728 — directory traversal / resource read in the file cache
Gradio SSRF CVE-2024-4325 and CVE-2024-47167 — /queue/join save_url_to_cache fetches attacker-controlled URLs (internal-network / cloud-metadata pivot)
Gradio /config discloses full component tree, app title, and analytics flags with no auth — schema map for automated exploitation
No rate limiting on inference/training — GPU compute exhaustion at operator cost; training jobs can be triggered by any visitor
Uploaded reference/training audio and trained .pth/.index models are readable/downloadable through the UI file components with no access control
risk_notes: RVC exists to clone a voice from as little as 10 minutes of audio; an open 7865 UI is a self-service impersonation factory. (1) Non-consensual voice cloning / biometric-identity theft — any visitor can upload a target's audio, train a model, and generate arbitrary converted speech in that voice. (2) Fraud / vishing enablement — converted speech drives voice-phishing, deepfake extortion, and CEO-fraud audio. (3) Training-data & model exposure — reference/training audio and trained .pth timbre models are the labeled voice datasets; they are downloadable through the Gradio file components and via the Gradio file-read CVEs (CVE-2023-51449 / CVE-2024-1561), so an attacker exfiltrates ready-made clone models plus /proc/self/environ secrets (HF tokens, cloud keys). (4) Compute theft — unauth GPU inference and training run at operator cost, trivially automated against /api/predict and /queue/join. (5) SSRF pivot — Gradio /queue/join save_url_to_cache reaches internal services and cloud-metadata endpoints. (6) --share tunnels defeat perimeter controls and put the whole UI on the public internet under a throwaway gradio.live hostname. The Gradio fingerprint (http.html:"gradio", /config) is shared with Applio and OpenVoice; disambiguate on RVC-specific tab/parameter labels (Model Inference, ckpt Processing, index rate, RMVPE).
deployment_notes: Python/conda or Docker on CUDA GPU hosts; the one-click Windows package (RVC-beta.7z) and Colab notebooks are the dominant install paths, so many exposed instances are hobbyist. Docker runs commonly bind server_name=0.0.0.0 and publish 7865. GPU-as-a-service (RunPod, Vast.ai, Kaggle, Colab-with-tunnel) deployments are frequent and often use --share, yielding public gradio.live URLs not visible to port scanners. HuggingFace Spaces host many RVC and RVC-derived demos, publicly indexed with no auth. The upstream default Gradio version has historically lagged, so exposed instances are commonly on Gradio 3.x/4.x branches vulnerable to the file-read and SSRF CVEs. Port 7865 is the convention but is configurable; other Gradio voice apps on 7860 can be RVC forks — confirm via /config component labels.
